K8KM: Aarti = {Skt. arati = waving lights before an image} placing flowers and a lit lamp on a tray, taking sandalwood and other fragrances, waving the tray before an idol and singing hymns in its praise — this is called the aarti of that idol. Murare = O Murari! {mur-ari; ari = enemy: the enemy of the demon Mur, a name of Krishna ji} O Parmatma!
O Prabhu! (Ignorant people perform aarti to idols, but for me) Your Name is (Your) aarti and bathing at the pilgrimage places.
Your Name, Lord, is my adoration and cleansing bath.
Your Name, O Lord, is my adoration in audience and ablution.
O Murari! Your Name alone is aarti for me, and the Name alone is (majan) bathing; the meaning is, there is no repetition like Your Name, and nothing so pure.
HR54: Pasare = displays, show {note: those shows are mentioned in the rest of the shabad: offering sandalwood, lamp, garland, food-offerings}. ||1||Rahau||
(O brother!) Missing Parmatma's Name, all other shows are false. ||1||Rahau||
Without the Name of the Lord, all ostentatious displays are useless. ||1||Pause||
Without the Lord's Name, all the ostentations are in vain. Pause.
O Hari! Without Your Name, all the displays of other rituals are false — that is, fruitless. ||1||Rahau||
YWQ6: Aasano = a cloth of wool or the like, sitting on which the idol is worshipped. Ursa = the stone slab for grinding sandalwood. Le = taking. Chhitkare = is sprinkled.

Your Name is (for me the pandit's) seat (sitting on which he worships the idol); Your Name alone is the slab (for grinding sandalwood); (the idol-worshipper dissolves saffron and) sprinkles saffron (on the idol), but for me Your Name alone is the saffron.
Your Name is my prayer mat, and Your Name is the stone to grind the sandalwood. Your Name is the saffron which I take and sprinkle in offering to You.
Your name is my prayer mat, Your name, my stone scraper and Your name the saffron, which I take and sprinkle for You.
Your Name alone is my seat, and Your Name alone is the (ursa) stone for grinding the tilak paste; and Your Name alone is the saffron — the uttering of it, received from the Guru, is the sprinkling.
AT7M: Ambhula = {Skt. ambhas = water} water. Jape = jap, having repeated. Tujhah kau = to You alone. Chare = is offered. ||1||

O Murari! Your Name alone is the water, the Name alone is the sandalwood; grinding (this sandalwood of the Name with the water of the Name), I apply to You the sandalwood of remembrance of Your Name. ||1||
Your Name is the water, and Your Name is the sandalwood. The chanting of Your Name is the grinding of the sandalwood. I take it and offer all this to You. ||1||
Your name is the water and Your Name and sandal. The repetition of Your Name is the grating of sandal. Taking the Name I offer it to You.
Your Name alone is the (ambhula) water, and the Name alone is Your sandalwood; grinding it by repetition, we take that very Name and offer it to You — that is, dedicate it to You. ||1||
0TZY: Bati = wick (of the lamp). Mah = in the lamp. Pasare = is poured.
O Prabhu! Your Name is the lamp, the Name alone is the wick (of the lamp), the Name alone is the oil that I have taken and poured in (the lamp of the Name);
Your Name is the lamp, and Your Name is the wick. Your Name is the oil I pour into it.
Your Name is the Lamp and Your Name the wick Taking the oil of Your name, I pour it therein.
Your Name alone is the lamp, and Your Name I have made the wick, and the (le) uttering of Your Name is the oil I have spread — that is, poured — into it.
45MP: Ujiaro = light. Saglare = all. Bhavan = in the worlds, in the realms. ||2||
I have lit the flame of Your Name alone (by whose blessing) there is light in all the worlds. ||2||
Your Name is the light applied to this lamp, which enlightens and illuminates the entire world. ||2||
Your Name is the light, which I have applied to the lamp and it has enlightened the whole world.
I have lit the (jot) fire of Your Name; by it the (ujiaro) light of wisdom has come in all the worlds. ||2||
NNKA: Taga = thread (for stringing a garland). Bhar atharah = all the vegetation: taking one leaf from every kind of plant in all the world's vegetation and gathering them makes 18 bhar; one bhar is five light maunds — an old notion handed down. Jootharre = soiled, because bees and the like have smelled them.

I have made Your Name the thread; I have made the Name the flowers and the garland of flowers; all other vegetation (from which people take flowers to offer before idols) is soiled (compared with Your Name).
Your Name is the thread, and Your Name is the garland of flowers. The eighteen loads of vegetation are all too impure to offer to You.
Your Name is the thread and Your Name the garland of flowers All the eighteen loads of vegetation are too impure to be offered to You.

Your Name alone is the thread, and the Name alone I have made the garland of flowers; apart from the Name, all the flowers of the eighteen loads of vegetation are (jootharre) soiled — that is, bumblebees and others take away their fragrance.
WQDP: Arpau = I offer. Tuhi = to You alone. Dholare = is waved.

(All this creation is made by You;) what can I place before You from what You have made? (So) I wave over You the whisk of Your Name alone. The meaning is: shows like aarti are false; remembrance alone is the right path of life. ||3||
Why should I offer to You, that which You Yourself created? Your Name is the fan, which I wave over You. ||3||
Why should I offered You, What You Yourself have made? Your Name is the fly-brush, which I wave over You.
What can I offer You from the things You Yourself have made? And Your Name alone is the whisk; and You alone are the one who waves the whisk, and it is waved over You alone. ||3||
92TA: Das atha = the 18 Puranas. Athsathe = the 68 pilgrimage places. Vartan = daily practice, pastime.

The daily practice of the whole world is this: (forgetting Your Name) people are absorbed in the stories of the eighteen Puranas, they have taken bathing at the sixty-eight pilgrimage places to be the meritorious deed, and so they are wandering through the life-forms of the four sources.
The whole world is engrossed in the eighteen Puraanas, the sixty-eight sacred shrines of pilgrimage, and the four sources of creation.
The whole world is engrossed in the eighteen Puranas, sixty-eight shrines and the four sources of creation.

The eighteen Puranas, the sixty-eight pilgrimage places and the four sources of life — the whole world's dealings are in these alone. Or: all the things that have been described above as being in use in all the world are the materials of the aarti.
Y1NA: Bhog = food-offering, an offering of milk, rice pudding and the like. ||4||3||
Ravidas says: O Prabhu! Your Name alone is (for me) Your aarti; I offer You the food-offering of Your ever-abiding Name alone. ||4||3||
Says Ravi Daas, Your Name is my Aartee, my lamp-lit worship-service. The True Name, Sat Naam, is the food which I offer to You. ||4||3||
Says Rav-Dass, Your name alone is my present worship. The True Name is the food which I offer You, O Lord.

Sri Ravidas ji says: O Hari! Your Name alone is aarti, and the True Name alone is the food offered to You; the meaning is, You accept only the repetition of the True Name. This alone is the cause of Your pleasure. ||4||3|| ☬ Trilochan the devotee, a merchant, remained without children. In old age he wished for a servant. Parmeshvar came and stayed as a servant. By his service he made the devotee and his wife very happy. One day the wife said to a neighbour: "We have taken on a servant who has been hungry since his sixth-day ceremony; he eats and is never full." Then, knowing Himself slandered, Parmeshvar vanished. Then, lamenting, the wife began to slander Parmeshvar: "The wretched Parmeshvar did not even let our servant stay." Then a voice came from the sky: "I stayed in your house as a servant. Because of your love I never said 'enough' to the food you gave. If you say so, I will come now." Hearing this, she repented instead. At the time when she was slandering, Trilochan ji, explaining the course of karma, says:

61E1: Ghrit = ghee. Saj = having arranged, having gathered.
(Being a sacrifice to You is) gathering incense, lamps and ghee (and the other) materials and doing Your aarti.
With incense, lamps and ghee, I offer this lamp-lit worship service.
I offer adoration prayers with incense, lamps and clarified butter.
Your praise as incense, the lamp of discernment and the ghee of love — in this way I have prepared the aarti.
AJTJ: Varne jau = I am a sacrifice. Kamlapati = the Husband of Lakshmi, Parmatma. ||1||
O Prabhu, Master of Maya! I am a sacrifice to You. ||1||
I am a sacrifice to the Lord of Lakshmi. ||1||
I am a sacrifice to the Lord of Lakhshmi.
O Vahiguru, Husband of Lakshmi! I am a sacrifice to You. ||1||
P8U8: Mangal = bliss, a joyful, auspicious observance.
Hail to You, Lord, hail to You!
Hail, to You, O God, hail;
O Ram, King of all! With mind, body and speech I ever sing Your auspicious songs in every way — that is, I praise You.
A5LE: Raja = Master. Ko = of (meaning, given by). ||1||Rahau||
O Ram! By Your grace there is always the bliss and joy (of remembering Your Name within me). ||1||Rahau||
Again and again, hail to You, Lord King, Ruler of all! ||1||Pause||
Eternal bliss is yours, O my Sovereign Lord, the Emperor. Pause.
Or: O Hari the King! Through the repetition of Your Name, Ram, there is ever joy for us in mind, body and speech. ||1||Rahau||
VTFC: Diara = a lovely little lamp. Nirmal = clean.
(For doing aarti) a lovely good lamp and a clean, pure wick too —
Sublime is the lamp, and pure is the wick.
The sublime lamp and pure wick are You,
Wisdom is the excellent (diara) lamp, and I have made a (nirmal) pure attention the wick.
7CM5: O Husband of Lakshmi! O Niranjan! For me You alone are [ ]. ||2||
You are immaculate and pure, O Brilliant Lord of Wealth! ||2||
(Tuhi) To know You as (niranjan) untouched by Maya — this alone is the lotus and the other flowers and the (pati) leaves for worship. Or: O Husband of Lakshmi! I have known You as pure. ||2||
B0PX: Rama bhagat = through devotion to Parmatma. Ramanand = {ram-anand} the bliss (of union with) Parmatma.
That person, by the blessing of devotion to the Prabhu, enjoys the bliss of union with Him,
Raamaanand knows the devotional worship of the Lord.
The Lord's meditation, Rama Nand, my Guru knows.
O Ram! Those who worship You alone know (ramanand) the bliss of rest — that is, the peace of withdrawal. Or: O Ram! My Guru, Ramanand ji, knows Your devotion.
9LE0: Pooran = all-pervading. Bakhanai = speaks, talks of. ||3||
who sings the virtues of the all-pervading Prabhu, whose form is supreme bliss. ||3||
He says that the Lord is all-pervading, the embodiment of supreme joy. ||3||
He describes the Lord as Omnipresent and the Embodiment of Supreme joy.
O perfect One, whose form is supreme bliss! They (bakhanai) utter Your praise — that is, they sing Your glory. ||3||
92M0: Madan moorat = a form that enraptures on sight, beautiful of form. Bhai tar = the one who carries across fears. Gobind = {go = creation; bind = to know, to care for} the one who cares for creation.
The Parmatma who is beautiful of form, who carries one across the fears (of the world), and who cares for creation —
The Lord of the world, of wondrous form, has carried me across the terrifying world-ocean.
The World Master of fascinating form has ferried me across the terrible world ocean.
O Madan — that is, beautiful form! Or: O Gobind! Carry me across this fearful world-ocean.
99C5: Bhanai = says. Bhaj = remember. Parmanande = the One who enjoys supreme bliss. ||4||2||
Sain says: (O my mind!) remember that Parmatma of supreme bliss. ||4||2||
Says Sain, remember the Lord, the embodiment of supreme joy! ||4||2||
Says, Sain, "Remember you, God, the Embodiment of Supreme joy".

Sri Sain ji says: O You whose form is supreme bliss! I am worshipping You. ||4||1|| ☬ Sri Pipa the devotee, from being king of Todarpur, became a disciple of Ramanand ji. Reflecting on the Vedantic teaching, he performs Hari's aarti in the form of oneness:
WTVT: Aarta = needy, suffering, a beggar {Skt. arta}.
O Prabhu, Sustainer of the earth! I am a beggar at Your door (fulfil my needs);
O Lord of the world, this is Your lamp-lit worship service.
O Lord, I perform Yours devotional worship.
O Gopal, sustainer of the (go) Vedas! Other people perform Your aarti, and I perform Your aarta — or, I am Your devotee in distress.
0S8Z: Whoever worships You — You bring their tasks to completion. ||1||Rahau||
You are the Arranger of the affairs of those humble beings who perform Your devotional worship service. ||1||Pause||
You arrangest the affairs of those persons who perform Yours devotional service. Pause.
For whoever worships You — You alone arrange their affairs. ||1||Rahau||
C5VR: Sidha = flour. Magau = I ask for.
I ask (from Your door) for lentils, flour and ghee,
Lentils, flour and ghee - these things, I beg of You.
I beg of You flour and ghee,
I ask for lentils, (sidha) flour, and ghee,
RMWN: that would keep my life happy every day;
My mind shall ever be pleased.
so shall my mind be ever pleased.
— food by eating which our soul may worship You gladly.
7LPV: Panhia = shoes {Skt. upanah}. Chhadan = clothing. Nika = fine.
I ask for shoes and fine clothing too,
I ask for (panhia) shoes to wear on the feet, and (nika) good (chhadan) clothes to wear on the body.
BJ91: Sat si ka anaj = grain from seven furrows, grain grown in a field ploughed seven times. ||1||
and I ask (from You alone) for grain from seven ploughings too. ||1||
And grain of seven kinds - I beg of You. ||1||
and corn of seven sorts, I beg of You.
And I ask for grain grown in land that has been (sat si ka) ploughed seven times. ||1||
XBFU: O Gopal! I ask (also) for a cow and a buffalo that give milk,
A milk cow, and a water buffalo, I beg of You,
The milch-cow and buffalo I ask for,
I ask for a cow and a buffalo that are laveri — that is, give milk.
P0F4: and I need a good Arab mare too.
and also a good Turkistani mare.
And I ask for a (turi) mare of (tajan) fine breed, for riding.
G1KU: A good wife at home too —
A good wife to care for my home
I ask for a good wife to look after my home.
And may the (gihan) wife of the house be good — that is, obedient.
BFR6: I, Your servant Dhanna, take by asking from You. ||2||4||
- Your humble servant Dhanna begs for these things, Lord. ||2||4||
Your slave Dhanna, O Lord, begs You to procure them.

Sri Dhanna ji says: I, Your servant, take by asking from You; give to me for the upkeep of the body. ||2|| ☬ That was the outward meaning. Now the inner, second meaning of this same shabad: O Gopal! I am (a) especially (rata) absorbed in Your Name — or Your true form. For the servants who worship You, You bring about their work, which is liberation. O Creator! (Dal) to crush — that is, destroy — the three afflictions, and to stay (sidha) facing You, and to stay (ghee) moist in Your love — this alone I ask from You. By this our (jiu) mind will ever be glad — that is, there will be bliss. To stay in Your refuge, and to (chhadan) cut the mind away from sense-objects, and to make the nature of the mind (nika) subtle — this I ask. And (anaj) today I ask for more: to speak (sat) truth and take up (sika) good conduct; or, O True Form, to stay content in Your (sika) coin — that is, Your command; and, (laveri) fixing my attention, filled with awe, to sing Your praise — this I ask. Through the turiya state, which is the highest, I ask for the vision of oneness in all people. And I ask for the intellect that (gihan) grasps the (ghar) true form, the intellect that is absorbed in the self. Sri Dhanna ji says: O Gopal! I, Your humble servant, take these things by asking from You, so …
